correctness.rationale: A cofinite semigroup with 3 pseudo-Frobenius must be closed under +3 on nonzero elements; for F>=4, 1,2,3 are gaps. Its three residue classes are therefore unique tails. Closure reduces to exactly b<=2a, a<=2b+1, c<=a+b+1; their maximal omitted elements give F and their gap numbers sum to a+b+c-1. Distinct residues force the three F-cases. A direct interval argument gives every genus coefficient; independent inclusion-exclusion sums give the cardinalities. Every finite case with 4<=F<=18 was enumerated without using tails, and counts and coefficients were checked through F=750. Finite checks corroborate, not replace, the proof.

originality.rationale: The current input is a natural infinite subfamily of a newly defined covariety. Three residue-tail thresholds yield a uniform exact genus generating polynomial, and a nontrivial lattice count produces a quadratic quasipolynomial with a residue-class phase change. Targeted research-record and accessible full-text checks found only general algorithms, distinct exact-PF constraints and other numerical-semigroup families, not a dominating explicit genus distribution. Historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: A different terminology for semigroups with the translation-by-three ideal property may contain an equivalent closed formula.

General algorithms already imply the possibility of computing each fixed F; novelty is only the explicit uniform all-F law and genus refinement.

value.rationale: The size and genus stratification of prescribed-pseudo-Frobenius covarieties are explicit goals of the motivating study. This theorem solves the entire natural infinite subfamily with smallest new prescribed positive gap 3, not an arbitrary numerical slice; genus is a principal invariant of numerical semigroups. The 3-class polyhedral constraint produces an exact coefficient formula, a quadratic quasipolynomial and a genuine 3:2 leading-coefficient phase distinction. No stronger theorem or application is claimed.
